claims.value: New prospective constraint: the next experiment is exactly one 30-minute dev-only alpha soak that must not change production or add durable controller persistence. Start with batch 128 as the ceiling while allowing fetch to adapt. Acceptance requires at least 900 PGCR/sec steady throughput during the final 10 minutes, zero integrity or recovery violations, no DB connection failure storm, and a successful controlled-stop restart from DB truth. answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint: split the three heavy machines across three level-0 Base Cores. No heavy-machine pair is safe to co-locate.

claims.value: The parent architecture is an Update-1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs network: protected core hubs, modular production cells, single-item rail lines and buffers, with every level-0 Base Core capped at 1,000 heat. The earlier monolithic mega-base was superseded.

The new explicit requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0 and Fire Wave protected. Heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 total across the factory, but placement is constrained per core by the 1,000 capacity. Constructorizer + Facturer = 1,150, and Facturer + Facturer = 1,300, so either co-location is unsafe and rejected. Amplifier figures remain disputed and are not credited.

Use three occupied level-0 core sites: Core A hosts the Constructorizer at 500 heat, leaving 500 capacity; Core B hosts Facturer 1 at 650 heat, leaving 350; Core C hosts Facturer 2 at 650 heat, leaving 350. If each site requires one Update-1 Wind Turbine v.1, the site totals become 600, 750, and 750 heat, leaving 400, 250, and 250 respectively. Rails add zero heat and can connect the distributed sites while conducting power. Existing buildings and all additional support equipment must fit inside those remaining per-core budgets.

Before construction, inspect and record each target core's current heat load and confirm the Constructorizer, Facturer, power source, recipes, and rail components are actually unlocked in Update 1. Build only when each complete site calculation—including existing load and support equipment—is at or below 1,000 heat, preferably with operational margin. Do not use hidden equipment, future Rail v.4/v.5, disputed amplifier capacity, or pre-Update-1 guidance.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next safe actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, and hand off complex work. It is not primarily a notes, transcript, retrieval, or memory-database product.

The earlier token result must not be interpreted as 2,932 uncached input tokens versus 1,070 equivalent BM25 tokens. The frozen BM25 regression baseline is one-shot top-k: 17/20 cases, 48/53 evidence items, and about 1,070 mean estimated tokens. The workspace recorded 17/20 cases, 46/53 evidence items, and 2,932 mean estimated tokens, but a multi-call workspace can replay prior snapshot/context through cache; the new gate therefore requires cumulative cached replay and uncached input to be reported separately before drawing a cost comparison. BM25 remains a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is one snapshot-pinned workspace transition: reopen a parent checkpoint at revision N; refresh it to N+1 with the changed evidence or constraint exposed as a diff; support exact plus lexical retrieval and a pluggable semantic path; batch typed query/read operations; and atomically commit an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent identifier and original source references. The implementation must use the checkpoint and delta without reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The measurable transition gate is: for every transition case, complete the reopen-refresh-diff-retrieve-read-child-commit flow in no more than four completed workspace calls; produce answer claims matching the direct-filesystem condition; preserve immutable parent-child lineage and source references; demonstrate snapshot pinning at N and refresh to N+1; exercise exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; and report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input. Failure of any lineage, claim-equivalence, call-count, diff, or token-accounting criterion blocks acceptance.

Provide exact and lexical retrieval immediately behind typed batched query/read operations, with semantic retrieval as a pluggable path.

Accept the slice only when each case uses at most four completed workspace calls, matches direct-filesystem answer claims, and reports cached replay separately from uncached input.
